COLLAPSE. Spring fires during green-up: burned dNBR raw -0.55 (negative), inverted vs US summer-fire training. dNBR-echo 0.609 = trivial all-positive baseline (thr0.1 recall1.0), not real discrimination. Both index & US model fail; needs native training (uljin F1 0.772).

conclusion: Generalization holds ACROSS BIOMES that share a summer/dry-season fire regime (positive dNBR): Mediterranean +0.16 -> boreal +0.065 -> eucalyptus +0.008 (value-add shrinks with domain distance, never collapses). It BREAKS ACROSS FIRE REGIMES: Korea spring fires imaged during vegetation green-up invert the dNBR burn signal (burned raw -0.55), so the feature the whole approach relies on carries no burn info -> both dNBR-echo and US model fail -> requires native/in-domain training (uljin achieved F1 0.772 natively). Onboard universal fire detection: dNBR baseline guaranteed only within summer/dry-season regimes; spring-fire regions (Korea/E.Asia) need in-domain training. Bottleneck confirmed as fire-regime/phenology domain shift + consistent multi-region real labels (Sen1Floods11 template).
